summary: Matthias Alexander Castrén worked in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Helsinki and the Imperial Alexander University around 1830 to 1836, later holding posts at both institutions from around 1851 to 1852.

Matthias de Vries was a linguist who studied at Leiden University from around 1838 to 1843. He held posts at the University of Groningen (1849–1853) and Leiden University (1853–1891), and taught Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern.

Matthias von Lexer worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at Graz, Berlin, and Erlangen-Nuremberg. He held posts at St. Anne's Gymnasium in Kraków (1855–1857), Freiburg (~1868–1870), Würzburg (1868), and Munich (1890).

Matthieu Ricard is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He earned a doctorate under François Jacob at the Pasteur Institute and studied with Kangyour Rinpoché and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, later serving on the Mind and Life Institute board.

Mattia Salvini is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He earned a PhD at SOAS under Tadeusz Skorupski and held posts at the International Buddhist College and Mahidol University (attested 2015).

Mauli Chand Prasad works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He completed a doctoral dissertation at Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar Bihar University under B. Jinanand and U. Dharmaratna, and served as a Lecturer in Pali at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (attested 1984).

Maurice Bloomfield was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Furman, Yale, and Johns Hopkins under William Dwight Whitney and Charles Rockwell Lanman. He spent his career as a professor at Johns Hopkins University from 1881 to 1926.

Maurice Frank Wiles was a religious studies scholar who studied at Cambridge. He held posts at Ridley Hall, the University of Ibadan, Clare College, and King's College London, before serving as Regius Professor of Divinity at Oxford from 1970 to 1991.

Maurice Grammont was a linguist who studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (circa 1886–1892) and under Ferdinand de Saussure. He held a post at the University of Montpellier from around 1905 to 1939.

Maurice Jametel worked in Sinology and Tibetology. He studied at the École nationale des langues orientales vivantes from around 1876 to 1880, later holding a post there from circa 1886 to 1889, where he taught Édouard Chavannes.
Maurice Leenhardt was a religious studies scholar who studied under Marcel Mauss. He later succeeded Mauss and held a post at the École Pratique des Hautes Études from circa 1940 to 1954.
Maurice O'Connell Walshe was a scholar in Buddhist studies and linguistics who studied under Walpola Rahula. He held a post at the Institute of Germanic and Romance Studies from around 1955 to 1979.

Maurine Stuart was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at the University of Manitoba and trained under Nadia Boulanger, Soen Nakagawa, Hakuun Ryoko Yasutani, and Eido Shimano. In 1979, she served as president and spiritual director of the Cambridge Buddhist Association.

Maurizio Taddei was a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He was a professor at the Italian Institute for the Middle and Far East and directed the editorial committee at the Italian Institute for Africa and the East.

Mauro Maggi specializes in Iranian and Central Asian studies and Tibetology. He earned his doctorate at the University of Naples "L'Orientale", served as Director at the Italian Institute for Africa and the East, and held a post at Sapienza University of Rome.

Mavis L. Fenn is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She earned degrees from Winnipeg, Calgary, and McMaster, and held posts at United College and the University of Waterloo, serving there as department chair (attested 2016).

Max Deeg specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He earned his PhD and Habilitation at the University of Würzburg, later holding posts at Cardiff University as Head of School and at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies as a research fellow.

Max Kaltenmark was a scholar of Sinology and religious studies who succeeded Henri Maspero. He served as director at the École française d'Extrême-Orient (1949–1953) and held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and the University of Paris (~1957–1979).

Max Leopold Margolis was a linguist and religious studies scholar who earned a PhD at Columbia. He held posts at Columbia, Hebrew Union College, UC Berkeley, and held the chair of biblical philology at Dropsie College from 1909 to 1932.
Max Lindenau was an Indologist who studied at the University of Leipzig until 1913 under Ernst Windisch.
